reason: The knob is live but it is not an independent axis. Live: c0 l.15, c1 guard patched by the builder, c2 l.47 -> CLI -> ILPSolver(appearance_weight), not hard-set in c3/c4. Not independent: in tracksdata 0.1.0rc9 the flow constraints (no merges) give #appear = #nodes - #edges and #disappear = #appear + #div. So the ILP objective = (A+Dis)*#appear + (Dis+Div)*#div - sum p*e, and the solution depends only on S = A+Dis (the fragment/start price) and the fork threshold Div - A. DOWN A=-0.2 (S 1.8, fork threshold 1.4 > max p = no forks) is the SAME ILP as ILP_DISAPPEARANCE_WEIGHT=1.8, i.e. a duplicate of the D-down arm. UP A=0.4 (S 2.4, fork threshold 0.8) is the SAME ILP as DISAPPEARANCE 2.4 + DIVISION 0.8, i.e. the diagonal of the D-up arm and a milder version of the pending exp85a (probe 50). A toy SCIP check confirmed both equivalences: identical node counts, and the solutions that differ are tied optima with equal objective. The fork half also has no direct output channel: filter_output_graph replaces all ILP edges with the 1:1 motion relink (0/56 lab fallbacks), the same caveat as 85a. The fragment half bites only on 4-5 node ILP fragments, because candidate edges have p >= 0.48 and output tracks shorter than 6 are dropped. Spending a slot here only confounds the two pure axes (the D pair and the division knob), which are already proposed or pending.
fixed_values: Do not probe APPEARANCE. Read the two pure ILP axes instead. Fragment axis: ILP_DISAPPEARANCE_WEIGHT 2.4 (UP) / 1.8 (DOWN), which is exactly what A +0.4 / -0.2 would have moved. Fork axis: ILP_DIVISION_WEIGHT, already pending in exp85a (0.4); if 85a reads UP, step 0.8/0.2.
